targets.query:
from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: -30s)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "notifications")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "state" or r._field == "severity" or r._field == "message")
  |> last()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["path"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> group()
  |> keep(columns: ["path", "state", "severity", "message"])
  |> sort(columns: ["severity"], desc: true)

from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: -5m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "propulsion" and r._field == "revolutions")
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _value: float(v: int(v: now()) - int(v: r._time)) / 1000000000.0 }))
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "_value"])

options.content:
**Not yet available.**

No physical ECU/SmartCraft interface is connected. This panel will show live ECU health and fault codes once SmartCraft CAN decoding is implemented (future milestone).

**Not yet available.**

No physical OpenCraft gateway hardware is deployed. This panel will show gateway health (uptime, CAN bus status, publish errors) once the SmartCraft gateway is implemented (future milestone).

**The two panels below show replayed historical capture data, not the live vessel.** They only populate while `services/replay` is running against a captured log such as `master-test01.log` -- see `docs/replay.md`. Every value is a raw or hypothesis-tagged CAN field candidate (see `docs/master-test01-analysis.md`), never a confirmed, calibrated decode. Check the Replay Status panel's `capture`/`state` columns before trusting anything in the Candidate Signals table.

targets.query:
from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: -30s)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "replay_status")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "state" or r._field == "position_s" or r._field == "duration_s" or r._field == "pct_complete" or r._field == "speed")
  |> last()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["capture"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> group()
  |> keep(columns: ["capture", "state", "speed", "position_s", "duration_s", "pct_complete"])

from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: -30s)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "can_replay")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "value" or r._field == "confidence_pct")
  |> last()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["hypothesis", "tier"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> group()
  |> keep(columns: ["hypothesis", "tier", "value", "confidence_pct"])
  |> sort(columns: ["tier", "hypothesis"])

options.content: **Every gauge below applies a labeled guess on top of the raw CAN value -- not a confirmed decode.** Scale/offset per candidate are in `services/replay/app/candidates.py` (`Guess`), each cited to a section of `docs/master-test01-analysis.md`. Hover a gauge's info icon for its specific basis -- some are fitted to a real field-sheet reading, some are pure unanchored placeholder assumptions (noted on each). A number here looking 'wrong' (e.g. Fuel reading ~2% when the real tank was ~100%) is itself useful evidence against that candidate/assumption, not a sign of a real state change.

panels.title: RPM (GUESS)
panels.description: Piecewise fit across 5 real anchor points: raw 0 -> 0 RPM (engine off), raw~4487 -> ~565 RPM (idle), raw~5960 -> 900 RPM, raw~6730 -> 1380 RPM, raw~7108 -> 2570 RPM (Gary's live observations, 2026-08-19 -- the 2570 anchor is the settled mean of a plateau that fluctuated before settling, so it's noisier than the others). Slope keeps accelerating across segments (0.13 -> 0.23 -> 0.62 -> 3.15 RPM/count) -- a single line fit none of them. Values above raw~7108 are extrapolated and are the least trustworthy part of this guess.

panels.title: Coolant Temperature (GUESS)
panels.description: GUESS, not a decode. Two-point fit: raw 5126 -> 95°F at key-on, raw 57642 -> 152°F at t=600s (section 6). Late-session instability in the report will show up as an erratic reading here too. Gauge shows a 10s rolling mean (not the single latest sample) since this candidate visibly jumps frame to frame.

panels.title: Oil Pressure (GUESS)
panels.description: Fitted from a single point (raw~84 at t=120s -> real 50.3 PSI) -- kept only because no better fit exists. Two rounds of live validation (2026-08-19) made this candidate's standing worse: it declines ~55% during idle while real oil pressure stays flat; and at the settled 2570 RPM plateau, where real oil pressure peaks at 65.9 PSI (the highest reading on the whole field sheet), this candidate's raw value is essentially the same as its own idle raw value -- it fails to rise at all across the confirmed RPM range. Tier downgraded from hypothesis to raw as a result. Treat this gauge as illustrative at best. Gauge shows a 20s rolling mean since this candidate visibly jumps frame to frame.

panels.title: Raw Water Pressure (GUESS)
panels.description: Piecewise fit across 5 real anchor points, all confirmed 2026-08-19: raw 256 -> 0 PSI (key-on), raw~34160 -> ~0.75 PSI (idle), raw~38905 -> 1.7 PSI (900 RPM), raw~42335 -> 2.8 PSI (1380 RPM), raw~45385 -> 4.1 PSI (settled 2570 RPM plateau). Slope accelerates with RPM -- roughly consistent with a centrifugal impeller pump, where pressure scales with speed squared. Encouraging new evidence, though section 8's other concerns (coarse quantization, onset-timing ambiguity with RPM) still stand.

panels.title: Fuel Level (GUESS)
panels.description: Flat 100% -- this candidate's raw value barely moves at all (4-5 the entire session), and Gary confirmed live (2026-08-19, 25% into a replay) real fuel was ~100% at that point too, matching the field sheet's 100% throughout. There isn't enough raw dynamic range to fit a scale, only an offset -- this guess can't tell a real constant-100% signal apart from any other near-constant byte, it just no longer contradicts the known value.

panels.title: Battery Voltage (GUESS)
panels.description: Anchored on raw 65284 -> 13.8V, confirmed live by Gary (2026-08-19, 25% into a replay, t~328s). This field only ever takes 2 distinct raw values in the whole capture; the OTHER state (5895) maps to ~10.2V under this same fit, which a real battery voltage should not do while running -- still evidence this candidate probably isn't a clean, continuous voltage signal, even though one of its two states now reads correctly.

panels.title: Trim (GUESS)
panels.description: Inverted 'byte range = 0-100%' guess, recentered so the observed ~239-240 raw 'down' baseline reads ~0% -- confirmed by both the field sheet (trim starts fully DOWN at key-on) and Gary's live observation (2026-08-19, 25% into a replay, expected ~0%). Direction is still a guess; magnitude during the trim-cycle window is not confirmed.

panels.title: Engine Hours/Minutes (GUESS)
panels.description: New structural finding, 2026-08-20 -- not one of the formal Phase 2 tool's 6 named hypotheses, so unscored (confidence -1) rather than percent-rated; see docs/master-test01-analysis.md section 3. Ticks up by exactly 1 count roughly every 59.58s (measured across 21 consecutive ticks: mean interval 59.576s, stdev 0.006s) -- a wall-clock-driven counter, categorically unlike every frame-driven counter elsewhere in this capture. Starts at raw 23 at key-on, so this is most likely a low byte of a continuously-accumulating engine-hours/run-time meter that was already at 23 when this capture began, not 'minutes since key-on'. Offset here just rebases the gauge to minutes elapsed since THIS capture started (0 at t~3s), not to any claimed absolute hour-meter value.

panels.title: Trim Direction (GUESS)
panels.description: New structural finding, 2026-08-20 -- not one of the formal Phase 2 tool's 6 named hypotheses, so unscored (confidence -1). Sits at 0 for the entire 22-minute file except for exactly 6 pulses (t=1033.3-1110.1s, straddling the field sheet's 22:59 mark) cleanly alternating between raw 1 and raw 2 -- an exact count/order match for the field sheet's 3 full up/down cycles. Mapped to +1 (Up) / -1 (Down) / 0 (idle) purely to match that documented order; which raw value is physically which direction is inferred, not independently confirmed. Distinct from the older, much weaker 'Trim (GUESS)' position gauge -- see docs/master-test01-analysis.md section 12.

panels.title: Oil Pressure (Inverse, GUESS)
panels.description: New leading oil-pressure candidate, found 2026-08-20 (170 rec 00 byte 3) after Gary asked whether a better one exists. Inversely tracks real oil PSI at every anchor: raw~39 at engine-off (0.5 PSI) -> raw~21 flat through the whole idle window (49.7 PSI) -> raw~15/12/11 at the confirmed 900/1380/2570 RPM plateaus (53.3/56.3/65.9 PSI). Cross-validated against a second, independent RPM test at the end of the file: bottoms out at the same raw value (11) at that run's RPM peak and returns to the same idle baseline (~20-21) afterward. Replaces the much noisier, non-tracking 'Oil Pressure (GUESS)' gauge as the leading candidate -- see docs/master-test01-analysis.md section 7.
